transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-11-18 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes | Attendees: Alex Park (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Aurelia ML), Mark O'Shea (Aurelia Infra), Sana Khan (Aurelia DS)

Auto-summary: quick run through of latest sensitivity numbers, discuss odd regressions on medical coding prompts, agree to run larger FP8 test with KV caching and to share heatmaps + updated configs.

[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda, we'll go over the model sensitivity matrix Priya prepared, then perf numbers with and without KV cache, and finally ops next steps. Jordan, you called out a couple of problem prompts last week so we'll look at those.

[00:29] Jordan (ML Eng): Yeah thanks. we saw a weird drift on some of the ICD mapping prompts when we switched to INT8. not all prompts, but like 4–5% accuracy hit on that slice, which is why we slowed the rollout.

[00:47] Priya (SE): Right — the sensitivity heatmap is in the deck I dropped in the slack thread, but quick summary: INT8 gives consistent 2.5–6% token-level perplexity lift on free-form clinical notes, FP8 is generally closer to fp16 baseline except for long-context summarization which shows a 1–3% delta. there are a few outliers on short, structured prompts (like ICD code mapping) where INT8 degrades more.

[01:15] Sana (Data Sci): just to be crystal, those numbers are on your test set or on our in-prod logs?

[01:22] Priya (SE): These are test harness results — 10k in-distribution prompts you gave us plus the 2k edge-suite you labeled. we did both batch and streaming-mode runs. note: streaming mode saw slightly worse deltas for INT8 — we think it's kv-cache alignment and quant noise compounding across steps.

[01:53] Mark (Infra): wait, kv-cache? you mean K V cache, our infra team spelled it K-V cash in the ticket earlier, so was confused — how big is that effect for latency?

[02:06] Priya (SE): sorry, yes KV cache. with KV cache enabled the per-token latency drops for repeated context by about 25–30% on average in FP8 and 20% in INT8 on our test harness because less compute per token plus fewer memory copies. However, cold starts (first tokens) are similar. throughput for FP8 with batching was up ~1.8x vs fp16; INT8 was up ~2.3x but with the noted quality regressions on the structured prompt slices.

[02:40] Alex (AE): And bucketed by p50/p95?

[02:44] Priya (SE): p50 is great — like 18–22ms per token on the 80B-equivalent model for FP8 with KV caching on our dedicated instance. p95 moves more, sometimes 80–140ms depending on burst. INT8 p95 was a touch better but not dramatically — gains are mostly in throughput.

[03:05] Jordan (ML Eng): the worry for us is those ICD mapping errors. small inaccuracies in codes = major downstream impact. are those recoverable via prompt engineering or do we need to stick to FP8 for that slice?

[03:18] Priya (SE): Good question. we tested a few approaches: prompt scaffolding (explicit constraints), temperature clamp, and selective fallbacks. Prompt scaffolding recovers about half of the delta for INT8; temperature clamp (0.0–0.2) helps reduce hallucination but impacts diversity. Selective fallbacks — routing structured prompts to FP8/FP16 — gives best net outcome: keep INT8 for most calls, route ICD-style prompts to FP8.

[03:52] Sana (Data Sci): routing sounds promising — what's the cost delta if we route 10% of calls to FP8 and 90% to INT8?

[04:02] Alex (AE): ballpark from our pilot numbers: that mix gives you about 35% cost reduction vs full FP8, and around 55% vs fp16 baseline. we'll send a more precise calc in the follow-up.

[04:16] Mark (Infra): any concerns about complexity? routing logic, extra latency on detection?

[04:22] Priya (SE): detection adds ~12–25ms depending on whether you do client-side tagging vs server-side classifier. Server-side adds a network hop but can be batched at the router and does not affect p95 much if you pipeline. We usually recommend lightweight client-side heuristics for high-throughput low-latency routes, and server-side for safer decisioning.

[04:46] Jordan (ML Eng): for now we can add a simple client-side header for ICD routes — low lift. but we want to see FP8 results with KV cache on a realistic 10k run.

[05:00] Priya (SE): Agreed — that's one of the action items. We'll run FP8 with KV cache on your 10k edge prompts including the ICD subset and report back.

[05:12] Alex (AE): switching gears — we also saw some strange variance at higher temperatures in FP8 on the long-context summarization tests?

[05:19] Priya (SE): yeah, the long-context summarization had small but visible ROUGE/semantic score variance at temps above 0.7. We hypothesize it's quantization noise amplified by multi-step autoregression length. We can mitigate with partial-precision (blend FP8 for attention matmuls and FP16 for the feed-forward) — it's a hybrid profile we can deploy as a model variant.

[05:46] Sana (Data Sci): can we get that hybrid as a canary? like 1% traffic to the hybrid, 99% to INT8?

[05:53] Priya (SE): yes, Redwood runtime supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback. we can set up a canary variant that uses FP8+blend and route a small share. If quality looks good we'll scale.

[06:05] Mark (Infra): curious on audit/security questions — if we use dedicated or private, we need SOC2 evidence and KMS integration. Are there blockers for on-prem?

[06:14] Alex (AE): no blockers; Redwood Private has KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. We'll attach the SOC2 report and the architecture diagram. Priya, can you point them to the security pack?

[06:25] Priya (SE): yes — I'll upload the security questionnaire and SOC2 link to the shared drive. note: on-prem deployment requires some network prep (ports, kernel modules in our packaging) — Mark we can set up a checklist for the infra runbook.

[06:40] Mark (Infra): great, we'll need that checklist. also want to run a smoke test for cold-start latencies.

[06:48] Alex (AE): added to action items.

[06:52] Priya (SE): quick note on tuning knobs that helped us: per-layer clip thresholds for INT8, per-head scaling, and selective outlier handling for norms. made a big diff on the structured prompts. we committed those configs in the pilot repo.

[07:12] Jordan (ML Eng): can you explain per-head scaling in plain words?

[07:16] Priya (SE): sure. some attention heads are numerically sensitive; scaling those heads separately before quantizing reduces quantization error. it's a light-weight transform during model prep.

[07:31] Sana (Data Sci): were any of the regressions tied to prompt length or tokenization idiosyncrasies?

[07:37] Priya (SE): yes, tokenization boundary effects show up — short structured prompts that tokenize to few subwords are more brittle under INT8. we flagged about 120 prompts in your edge-suite that are high-risk.

[07:52] Jordan (ML Eng): ok — let's see the flagged list. we'll probably normalize some of those inputs on our side before routing.

[07:59] Alex (AE): on the operations side, Priya mentioned runtime knobs for autoscaling; want to call that out — dedicated pools vs hosted burst — what's recommended for pilot?

[08:10] Priya (SE): for the pilot we recommend dedicated small pool with burst enabled. dedicated gives predictable p95 and capacity for the hybrid FP8/INT8 routing. bursting helps during spikes. For cost-savings, keep lower min replicas and configure aggressive batch windows. we'll share recommended autoscale yaml.

[08:30] Mark (Infra): how do upgrades/rollouts look? we need canary rollback steps documented if we hit regressions.

[08:38] Priya (SE): Redwood Console supports canary/A B rollouts with automatic rollback on quality/regression alerts tied to your eval set. we can wire your ICD test set in as a monitoring suite and trigger auto-fallback to FP8 if the error rate crosses threshold.

[09:00] Sana (Data Sci): and what's the detection latency for a regression? I mean, how many calls before an alert?

[09:06] Priya (SE): configurable. typical default is 1000 calls with a sliding window for stats; we can lower that threshold for high-sensitivity workflows.

[09:18] Jordan (ML Eng): good. last technical ask from our side — we want a reproducible exact-step script to reproduce the INT8 artifacts locally on a dev box so our data team can iterate.

[09:27] Priya (SE): we'll provide the quantization packaging script and model artifact pins. it's the usual flow: quantize with provided scale tables + per-head scale transform, then run the eval harness. I'll push to the pilot repo.

[09:40] Alex (AE): ok let's surface the concrete next steps and owners — quick recap?

[09:46] Jordan (ML Eng): run larger FP8+KV cache test and share results (Jordan assigned?)

[09:51] Priya (SE): actually Redwood will run the FP8+KV run on the 10k edge prompts — Priya to run and share.

[09:57] Alex (AE): Alex will update pricing and routing cost model and share a spreadsheet.

[10:03] Mark (Infra): we'll get network checklist and plan for on-prem smoke run week of 11/30.

[10:11] Sana (Data Sci): we'll review flagged prompts and normalize the short tokenization ones.

[10:19] Priya (SE): final note: we'll also spin up a 1% hybrid canary for long-context summarization to see hybrid FP8/FP16 interpolation effects.

[10:31] Alex (AE): perfect. any other questions?

[10:35] Jordan (ML Eng): no, thanks everyone.

[10:37] Alex (AE): thanks all. we'll share the sensitivity heatmap + configs and the FP8+KV run results by Friday.

[10:45] End meeting.

Notes on transcription: speaker turns occasionally misattributed by auto-transcribe, some technical acronyms spelled out (F P 8) or mis-joined, and proper names may be slightly off.
